The four parts of your goal are all working. Before locking scope, let me walk you through the **boundary situations** so we agree how the app should behave in them.

I've set up a **separate demo view with sample data** (it won't touch your real bookmarks) so you can see these states directly:

**http://maker:4001/?demo=edge**

Please look at these specific things there:

1. **A very long title, description, address, and a very long tag** — top item. Check the title trims to one line, the description trims after two lines, and nothing pushes the card out of shape.
2. **A bookmark with no description** (2nd item) — confirm it just omits the line cleanly, no empty gap.
3. **A bookmark with no tags** (3rd item) — confirm it looks fine without a tag row.
4. **A long list (120+ items)** — scroll and confirm it stays readable; the count at the top reflects the total.

Now on your **real app** (**http://maker:4001**), please check the **fetch-failure** case:

5. Save a link the app can't read details from — paste `https://broken.example.com/some-article` and Save. You should see a gentle notice that details couldn't be fetched, with a title guessed from the address and an empty description you can fill in yourself — and you can still save it.

And two behaviour questions (no visual needed):

- When the list gets **very large**, are you happy relying on **search and tag filters** to find things (with a simple scroll otherwise), or would you expect something more like paging or grouping?
- If you paste an address **without the `http://` part** — just `example.com` — should the app **assume `https://`** and accept it, or require you to include it?

There's no time-based behaviour in this app (nothing expires or changes by time of day), so there are no time-related boundaries to check — tell me if you think otherwise.
